scores.evidence: Async pull-based GitOps. CI writes a digest bump to the environment repo, and Argo CD pulls and applies it. CI never holds cluster credentials.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (OIDC, cosign keyless, digest pinning, expand/contract, Kyverno verifyImages) are accurate; minor imprecision such as calling rolling deploys 'automatic rollback' and 'same-SHA rebuild gives same digest' hedged, and keyless signing with public Rekor for private code is unexamined.

scores.evidence: Buy/OSS the engines... Build only the glue: templates, service manifest schema, onboarding generator, promotion policy.
scores.rationale: Covers core needs with explicit deferrals, but no service inventory survey, and the Kubernetes-only target is stated rather than surveyed, plus test environments are thin.

scores.evidence: Git (the GitOps repo) is the single record of which artifact version runs in each environment.
scores.rationale: Consistent choices (digest-only, pull GitOps, trusted/untrusted pools, ring rollouts) are honored across phases and cross-cutting table; no notable contradictions.

scores.evidence: A deliberately broken template release is caught and halted in the pilot ring before reaching ring 2.
scores.rationale: Measurable, risk-targeted exit checks (injected 5xx rollback, unsigned image rejected, migration rollback rehearsal) are early-ish, though thresholds like 15 min are unjustified and production validation of pipelines is mostly dashboards.

scores.evidence: Deploy target (stated, not assumed): Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/AKS), one staging cluster and one prod cluster to start.
scores.rationale: Revisit triggers exist for many decisions but the key inputs (team size, commit volume, existing stack, compliance) are not stated, and thresholds like 30% and 15% are invented without labeling.

scores.evidence: One bad change can break 50. That is why template rollout rings come first in this phase.
scores.rationale: Covers bad template, compromised credentials, unsigned images, bad releases, cache failure, GitHub outage, DR; flaky tests, fork-PR abuse specifics and secret leakage from logs are thin.

scores.evidence: Platform SLOs and on-call. CI availability at least 99.5%, queue p95, Argo sync lag.
scores.rationale: Rollback, monitoring, drift alert, migration pattern, break-glass and on-call are concrete, but named ownership arrives only in Phase 5 and the platform team's size isn't addressed.
Cost appears only as a Phase 6 item and revisit triggers; no estimate of build volume or compute cost, and self-hosted vs hosted is chosen without numbers.

scores.evidence: Signing keys | Keyless cosign through OIDC (Fulcio/Rekor). | Air-gapped or sovereignty requirements → keys held in a KMS
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a revisit trigger and exit path, with additive-only schema versioning and the costly identity/contract decisions placed first and validated with pilots.

scores.evidence: Full Backstage developer portal (plugins, TechDocs) | More than 10 teams
scores.rationale: Buys engines, defers monorepo, previews, multi-cluster; some weight like SLSA L3, chaos tests and DORA dashboards is arguable but phased late.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 ... git push of commit abc123 ... GET https://<svc>.prod/version returns abc123
scores.rationale: Concrete first slice, dependency-justified ordering, checkable exit criteria per phase, and triggers for adapting.

checklist.evidence: Keep the existing polyrepo. One central set of versioned, reusable pipeline templates. No per-team custom pipelines.
Each runs in shadow mode first (the new pipeline builds alongside the legacy one), then cuts over.
Build once, promote the same digest. Images are immutable and referenced by digest (sha256), never by mutable tag.
GitHub→cloud OIDC with zero static secrets; ... Separate runner pools for untrusted work (fork PRs) and trusted work
Keyless cosign signature and SLSA provenance attestation on every image.
Expand/contract migrations run as a pre-sync job. Every deploy must be rollback-safe.
Service manifest schema... Versioned, with additive changes only.
BuildKit registry cache plus a remote dependency cache keyed by lockfile hash.
self-hosted ephemeral runners on Kubernetes (Actions Runner Controller)
Platform SLOs and on-call. CI availability at least 99.5%, queue p95, Argo sync lag.
A promotion PR to the prod overlay needs one human approval. CODEOWNERS on environment directories; audited break-glass

traps.evidence: Decommission each legacy pipeline after 2 clean weeks, and revoke its credentials.
Images are immutable and referenced by digest (sha256), never by mutable tag.
GitHub→cloud OIDC with zero static secrets
Each release goes pilot ring → 20% → all.
Custom CI orchestration engine | Effectively never.

note: Strong, dependency-ordered, reversible-aware GitOps plan with a real pilot and safe rollout; weak on cost estimation, service inventory, test environments/flaky tests and stated scale assumptions.
